title: AWL Sublist 4
description: Cuarta sublista de la Academic Word List: 60 familias útiles para investigar, comparar datos y matizar argumentos.

cards.definition: The right or opportunity to use or reach something; to reach or get.
cards.example: Millions of people still lack access to clean drinking water.
cards.warning: Como verbo no lleva 'to': 'access the website', no 'access to the website'. Como sustantivo sí: 'access to'.

cards.definition: Enough or good enough for a particular purpose.
cards.example: Many workers do not receive adequate training.
cards.warning: 'Adequate' significa sobre todo 'suficiente'; 'adecuado' (apropiado) suele ser 'appropriate' o 'suitable'.

cards.definition: Happening once a year, or calculated over one year.
cards.example: The country's annual growth rate fell to 1.5%.

cards.definition: Easy to see or understand; seeming to be true but possibly not.
cards.example: It soon became apparent that the policy was not working.
cards.warning: 'Apparent' suele significar 'evidente', no solo 'aparente'. 'Apparently' = 'al parecer, por lo visto'.

cards.definition: Close to the exact number but not completely accurate; to come close to a number or quality.
cards.example: The approximate cost of the project is £2 million.
cards.note: En IELTS Task 1 es muy útil: 'approximately one third'.

cards.definition: The way you think or feel about something, shown by your behaviour.
cards.example: Public attitudes towards recycling have changed dramatically.
cards.warning: Es 'attitude towards/to', no 'attitude with/about' en registro académico.

cards.definition: To say something is caused by something; a quality or feature.
cards.example: The fall in crime has been attributed to better street lighting.

cards.definition: Relating to ordinary citizens, not the military or religion; polite.
cards.example: Civil society organisations play an important role in democracy.
cards.warning: 'Civil servant' = funcionario. 'Civilisation' no pertenece a esta familia en la AWL.

cards.definition: A set of rules; a system of symbols; to write computer instructions.
cards.example: All employees must follow the company's code of conduct.

cards.definition: To do something wrong; to promise to do something; to give fully.
cards.example: The government has committed to reducing emissions by 50%.
cards.warning: 'Commit to + -ing': 'committed to reducing', no 'committed to reduce'. 'Comprometido' (prometido en matrimonio) es 'engaged'.

cards.definition: To share information, ideas or feelings with others.
cards.example: Effective leaders communicate their goals clearly.

cards.definition: To focus all your attention; to be gathered in one place.
cards.example: Wealth is increasingly concentrated in the hands of a few.
cards.warning: Es 'concentrate on', no 'concentrate in' (salvo 'concentrated in' = agrupado en un lugar).

cards.definition: To discuss with others; to give an official title or advantage.
cards.example: A university degree confers significant advantages in the job market.
cards.warning: 'Conferencia' (charla única) suele ser 'lecture' o 'talk'; 'conference' es un congreso.

cards.definition: A clear difference between things; to compare to show differences.
cards.example: In contrast to the city, the countryside saw its population decline.
cards.warning: Es 'in contrast to/with', no 'in contrast of'. 'Contrastar' información = 'check/verify', no 'contrast'.

cards.definition: A series of events that repeat in the same order; to ride a bicycle.
cards.example: Poverty can become a cycle that passes from one generation to the next.

cards.definition: A discussion in which people express different opinions; to discuss.
cards.example: There is ongoing debate about the benefits of homework.
cards.warning: Como verbo es transitivo: 'debate the issue', no 'debate about the issue'.

cards.definition: Without being affected by something; even though something is true.
cards.example: Despite rising costs, demand for higher education continues to grow.
cards.warning: Nunca 'despite of'. Va con sustantivo o -ing, no con oración: 'despite being', 'despite the fact that'.

cards.definition: A measurement such as length or height; an aspect of a situation.
cards.example: The crisis has an important social dimension.

cards.definition: Relating to one's own country, or to the home and family.
cards.example: Domestic flights produce more emissions per passenger than trains.
cards.warning: 'Domestic' en economía significa 'nacional': 'domestic demand' = demanda interna.

cards.definition: To appear or become known; to come out from somewhere.
cards.example: A clear pattern emerges from the survey results.
cards.warning: 'Emergency' (emergencia) comparte raíz pero no pertenece a esta familia. En textos académicos 'emerge' suele significar 'surgir' o 'salir a la luz' ('it emerged that...').

cards.definition: A mistake.
cards.example: Human error was the main cause of the accident.

cards.definition: Relating to a group of people with a shared culture, language or origin.
cards.example: London is home to people from hundreds of ethnic groups.
cards.warning: No confundir con 'ethical' (ético).

cards.definition: Something you hope to achieve.
cards.example: The main goal of the programme is to reduce child poverty.

cards.definition: Money given for a purpose, e.g. study; to officially give or allow.
cards.example: Students from low-income families may be granted financial support.
cards.warning: 'Take something for granted' = dar algo por sentado.

cards.definition: For this reason; as a result.
cards.example: The process is expensive and, hence, rarely used.
cards.warning: 'Hence' puede ir sin verbo: 'Fuel prices rose; hence the protests.' No uses 'hence why' en registro formal.

cards.definition: An idea that explains something but has not yet been proven.
cards.example: The results support the hypothesis that stress affects memory.

cards.definition: To put a plan, system or decision into action.
cards.example: The reforms were implemented gradually over five years.

cards.definition: To show that someone or something is involved in a crime or problem.
cards.example: Several genes have been implicated in the disease.
cards.warning: 'Implicate' tiene matiz negativo (culpa). 'Implicar' neutro = 'involve'.

cards.definition: To officially force a rule, tax or punishment on someone.
cards.example: Many countries impose taxes on sugary drinks.
cards.warning: Es 'impose X on Y': 'impose a tax on drinks'.

cards.definition: To combine parts into a whole; to become part of a group or society.
cards.example: Language classes help immigrants integrate into their new communities.

cards.definition: Inside something, such as the body, a country or an organisation.
cards.example: The company carried out an internal review of its practices.

cards.definition: To examine a crime, problem or statement carefully to find the truth.
cards.example: This study investigates the effects of noise on concentration.
cards.warning: Para 'hacer investigación científica' en general se usa 'do research'; 'investigate' es examinar algo concreto.

cards.definition: Paid work that someone does regularly; a task.
cards.example: Automation may lead to the loss of millions of jobs.
cards.warning: 'Job' es contable (a job); 'work' es incontable (some work).

cards.definition: A piece of paper with information on a product; to describe in a fixed way.
cards.example: Food labels should show sugar content clearly.

cards.definition: A part of a machine; a system or process that achieves a result.
cards.example: There is no mechanism for students to report problems anonymously.

cards.definition: Easy to see, notice or understand.
cards.example: The most obvious solution is not always the most effective.
cards.warning: En ensayos evita abusar de 'obviously': puede sonar poco académico o condescendiente.

cards.definition: To fill a space or time; to live in or use a place; to take control.
cards.example: Women occupy only a small proportion of senior positions.
cards.warning: 'Occupation' también significa 'profesión'. 'Estar ocupado' es 'be busy', no 'be occupied'.

cards.definition: A choice between possibilities.
cards.example: For many students, studying online is the only realistic option.

cards.definition: The amount of goods or work produced.
cards.example: Industrial output rose by 3% in the last quarter.

cards.definition: Considering everything; in total.
cards.example: Overall, the number of tourists increased between 2000 and 2020.
cards.note: Clave para el 'overview' de IELTS Task 1: 'Overall, it is clear that...'.

cards.definition: Happening at the same time or similar; a similarity.
cards.example: The rise in obesity runs parallel to the growth of fast food.

cards.definition: A limit or set of rules that controls how something is done.
cards.example: The study was conducted within strict ethical parameters.

cards.definition: A stage in a process; to introduce or remove gradually.
cards.example: Petrol cars will be phased out over the next decade.

cards.definition: To say what will happen in the future.
cards.example: Experts predict that demand for electricity will double by 2050.
cards.note: Útil en IELTS Task 1 con gráficos de proyecciones: 'It is predicted that...'.

cards.definition: Most important; the head of a school or college.
cards.example: The principal cause of the decline was a lack of investment.
cards.warning: No confundir con 'principle' (principio). Mismo sonido, distinta palabra.

cards.definition: Existing or happening before something else.
cards.example: No prior experience is required for the course.
cards.warning: 'Prior to' = 'before' (más formal). Evita 'prior than'.

cards.definition: Relating to a skilled job requiring training; a person with such a job.
cards.example: Health professionals warn about the risks of excessive screen time.

cards.definition: A planned piece of work; to estimate future amounts.
cards.example: The population is projected to reach 10 million by 2040.

cards.definition: To encourage or support something; to move someone to a higher job.
cards.example: Schools should promote healthy eating habits.

cards.definition: A government, especially an unfair one; a system of rules or treatment.
cards.example: The new tax regime favours small businesses.
cards.warning: 'Estar a régimen' (dieta) es 'be on a diet', no 'be on a regime'.

cards.definition: To find a solution to a problem; to decide firmly.
cards.example: The two sides failed to resolve their differences.

cards.definition: To keep or continue to have something.
cards.example: Companies struggle to retain skilled staff.

cards.definition: A number of similar things that follow each other.
cards.example: The government has introduced a series of measures to reduce crime.
cards.warning: 'Series' es igual en singular y plural: 'a series', 'two series'.

cards.definition: A number that represents a fact; (statistics) the science of collecting and analysing numerical data.
cards.example: Official statistics show a sharp rise in youth unemployment.

cards.definition: Social or professional position; the official position or situation.
cards.example: In many cultures, owning a car is a symbol of social status.

cards.definition: Mental pressure or worry; to emphasise something.
cards.example: The report stresses the importance of early education.

cards.definition: Happening after something else.
cards.example: Subsequent studies confirmed the original findings.

cards.definition: An amount of money; the total of numbers; to summarise.
cards.example: Governments spend large sums of money on defence.

cards.definition: A short statement giving the main points of something.
cards.example: The final paragraph provides a brief summary of the main arguments.
cards.warning: 'Summary' es resumen; 'résumé' en EE. UU. es currículum.

cards.definition: To take on a task or responsibility and start doing it.
cards.example: Few students undertake work experience before graduating.
cards.warning: Irregular: undertake – undertook – undertaken. 'Emprendedor' es 'entrepreneur', no 'undertaker' (que significa 'funerario').
